name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Huge GOP fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Open seat removes incumbent effect but doesn't close the partisan gap
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, the Republican nominee's $2M-plus in fundraising and outside support against a Democratic candidate with minimal resources, and markets pricing a GOP win near 95% all point the same direction. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or a major Democratic outside-spending surge would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Houston-area seat leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of R+13. Morgan Luttrell's retirement leaves the seat open, but the Republican nominee, Jessica Hart Steinmann, has raised over $2 million and benefits from roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised about $22,000 with no reported outside spending.

Prediction markets give the Republican nominee about a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong Republican lean and the lopsided resource gap, pointing to a comfortable Republican hold.
